emergencyNumber: 112 or 999 (both connect to ambulance, police, fire — 112 is EU-wide standard, 999 is the traditional UK/Irish number)
healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private system. Residents have access to a two-tier public system (Medical Card / GP Visit Card). Tourists from EU/EEA countries covered by EHIC. Others pay out-of-pocket.
qualityNotes: High-quality healthcare with well-trained doctors. The public health system (HSE) is good but can have long wait times for non-emergency care. Private healthcare is widely available and more expensive but offers faster access. English is universally spoken. Dublin has several international clinics.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open Mon-Sat 9am-6pm, some late-night pharmacies in cities. Look for 'Pharmacy' or 'Chemist' signs. Some pharmacies open Sunday in city centers.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacists are well-trained and helpful. Many common OTC medications are available. EU prescriptions are accepted. Some medications available OTC in other countries require prescriptions in Ireland. Emergency contraception is available without prescription from pharmacies.
prescriptionRules: EU prescriptions are accepted. Prescriptions from outside Ireland may need verification by an Irish doctor. Ireland follows EU pharmaceutical regulations. Some medications have different legal status than in other countries.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine products (like Nurofen Plus) require a prescription in Ireland above small quantities. Some codeine preparations are available OTC in small doses, but higher-strength products require prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines (Valium, Xanax, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. EU regulations apply. Carry doctor's letter and original prescription. Customs inspections occur for controlled substances.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Requires Irish prescription or special license. Contact the Irish Health Products Regulatory Authority (HPRA) before traveling with ADHD medications. Carry full documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Medical cannabis is legal in Ireland under specific circumstances via the Medical Cannabis Access Programme, but it's highly restricted. Recreational cannabis is illegal. CBD products with <0.2% THC are legal.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. EU citizens should carry EHIC. Non-EU travelers should carry original prescriptions and multilingual medical certificates. For controlled substances, carry a Schengen-style certificate if available.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not required but strongly recommended for all travelers.
travelInsurance.tips: Ireland is expensive for healthcare. A hospital emergency room visit can cost 100-200 EUR without insurance. Doctor visits cost 50-80 EUR. Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is essential — Ireland's geographic isolation makes medical evacuation costly. EHIC covers EU citizens for emergency care.

recommended: meningococcal disease (for students/young adults in close quarters)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Ireland has seen mumps outbreaks in recent years — ensure MMR vaccination is up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Ireland. Irish tap water is among the cleanest in the world.
foodSafetyTips: Ireland has excellent food safety standards. Traditional foods like fish and chips, Irish stew, and soda bread are safe. Irish dairy and beef are world-class. Be cautious with unfamiliar wild plants. Food in pubs is generally safe.
medicalTourismNote: Ireland is not a major medical tourism destination due to high costs. However, Dublin has specialist medical centers for certain treatments. Medical tourists typically come for specialized consultations rather than procedures due to cost.
